37 /**
38 * @brief Lazy unary expression for nda::Array types.
39 *
40 * @details A lazy unary expression contains a single operand and a unary operation. It fulfills the nda::Array
41 * concept and can therefore be used in any other expression or function that expects an nda::Array type.
42 *
43 * The only supported unary operation is the negation operation ('-').
44 *
45 * @tparam OP Char representing the unary operation.
46 * @tparam A nda::Array type.
47 */
48 template <char OP, Array A>
49 struct expr_unary {
50 static_assert(OP == '-', "Error in nda::expr_unary: Only negation is supported");
51
52 /// nda::Array object.
53 A a;
54
55 /**
56 * @brief Function call operator.
57 *
58 * @details Forwards the arguments to the nda::Array operand and negates the result.
59 *
60 * @tparam Args Types of the arguments.
61 * @param args Function call arguments.
62 * @return If the result of the forwarded function call is another nda::Array, a new lazy expression is returned.
63 * Otherwise the result is negated and returned.
64 */
65 template <typename... Args>
66 256 auto operator()(Args &&...args) const {
67 512 return -a(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
68 }
69
70 /**
71 * @brief Get the shape of the nda::Array operand.
72 * @return `std::array<long, Rank>` object specifying the shape of the operand.
73 */
74 16 [[nodiscard]] constexpr auto shape() const { return a.shape(); }
75
76 /**
77 * @brief Get the total size of the nda::Array operand.
78 * @return Number of elements contained in the operand.
79 */
80 [[nodiscard]] constexpr long size() const { return a.size(); }
81 };
